title.quote: Learning From the Past with Cascading Eligibility Traces
title.justification: Title as given at the top of the paper
title.value: Learning From the Past with Cascading Eligibility Traces

extractions.description: The paper proposes cascading eligibility traces (CETs), eligibility traces formed by a state-space model inspired by biochemical cascades, to handle delayed credit assignment signals in models of synaptic plasticity. The authors test CETs on supervised image classification (MNIST, CIFAR-10) and reinforcement learning (CartPole, LunarLander, MinAtar/SpaceInvaders) under behaviorally relevant delays and extremely long retrograde-signaling delays, measuring accuracy, episodic return, and gradient cosine alignment.

type.quote: We present a series of results that demonstrate the utility of CETs for credit assignment with biologically realistic delays.
type.justification: The paper runs simulations/experiments on datasets and RL environments, with some analytic derivations in appendix.
